newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bank lending rises seven pct in April.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bank lending rises seven pct in April.

text.p: Venezuelan commercial bank lending rose 7.0 percent in April to 2.82 trillion bolivars ($5.8 billion dollars), easing slightly from March's galloping 9.4 percent rate, Softline consultants reported.
According to the firm's monthly round-up of 40 commercial banks, total deposits rose at the slower rate of 5.69 percent to 5.58 trillion bolivars.
The quicker rise in loans pushed up the banking sector's intermediation index -- which describes the amount banks lend per each bolivar deposited -- to 47.05 percent, the highest since mid-1994.

In a further sign of a shift of bank portfolios into loans, total investments in securities edged ahead only 1.17 percent to 2.82 trillion bolivars. Over the past two years of recession and restrained borrowing, such investment have served as a refuge for Venezuela's liquidity rich banks.
As a percentage of bank assets, investments in securities dropped one percentage point to 35 percent in April, while loans rose one and a half points to 38.5 percent of bank assets, Softline said.
Softline added that bank capitalization rates, or the ratio of shareholders equity to total assets, slipped to 13.64 percent from March's 13.8 percent rate.

Last week Central Bank governor Antonio Casas Gonzalez said Venezuela's banking system, only recently recovered from the 1994-95 financial crisis, needed to further increase capitalization levels if it was to keep up with growing credit demand.
Loan demand is expected to increase as economic recovery sets in, with the government forecasting four percent growth for this year, and five for the next.
State-owned oil giant Petroleos de Venezuela's 10-year plan envisions annual investment of some $6 billion alone.
